rows.subtype: Approach: generates a big list first and judges it afterwards [Action]
rows.description: A group planning a school skit writes twenty story ideas without arguing, then crosses out those needing too many props, and keeps three to try out.

rows.subtype: Approach: generates ideas alone before sharing so early voices do not dominate [Thinking]
rows.description: A club captain asks members to jot ideas silently for five minutes before discussion, and a shy member's suggestion for a quiz format becomes the choice.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 18–22, 23–26

rows.subtype: Approach: criticises ideas during the generating phase and cuts the flow [Pitfall]
rows.description: In a college brainstorm, someone says that will never work after each idea, and soon nobody speaks. Only safe, familiar suggestions reach the list.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 23–26

rows.subtype: Approach: separates a generation round from a selection round with agreed criteria [Revision]
rows.description: A product manager notices a stalled meeting, sets ten minutes of no-criticism ideas, then applies three criteria, cost, time and user need, to pick candidates.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22

rows.subtype: Approach: reframes the problem to use an unexpected feature [Thinking]
rows.description: A boy cannot reach a ball under a sofa with his hand. He reframes it from reaching to pushing it out, and uses a long ruler from his bag.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A student sure he needs a big table to display his model realises the display could hang from the wall. The assumption of needing a table was never a real rule.

rows.subtype: Approach: changes the question from making it faster to removing the step [Action]
rows.description: Instead of speeding up a manual attendance sheet, a student volunteer replaces it with a QR check-in that removes the copying step altogether.

rows.subtype: Approach: turns a clever reframe into a plan that ignores practical limits [Pitfall]
rows.description: A young founder reframes a delivery problem as a barter network, an interesting idea, but does not test whether neighbours would actually trade or trust it.

rows.subtype: Approach: keeps the fresh idea and tests it with one small pilot [Revision]
rows.description: Told the barter idea is untested, she runs a two-week trial in one lane and learns which parts people accept, then adjusts the idea from evidence.

rows.subtype: Approach: postpones a heated decision until emotions settle [Action]
rows.description: After a quarrel with a friend, a teenager drafts an angry message but waits a night. By morning he writes a calmer note asking to talk.
